      "observations": [
        "All eight owned diffs and relevant current module/native consumers/UI/test contracts read. This first patch removes the one-attachment nsIMessenger API, introduces JS detach/delete workflows and migrates a subset of callers. Original multi-attachment UI paths still use native detachAllAttachments; accepted UI later uses AttachmentInfo everywhere. The constructor keeps necko attachment URLs distinct from message URIs.",
        "The asynchronous completion sequence is strip, replacement copy, delete old message, then IMAP refresh. Key-change observation occurs inside setMessageKey before copy onStopCopy; the extension test now waits for the whole deleteAttachments promise before requesting the old extension ID. Its subject/deleted-part/name assertions exercise payload and ID lookup; IMAP/NNTP are skipped and all seven Browser.test.assertEq calls in that affected task lack messages.",
        "stripAttachments filters out descendants and missing part IDs by mutating the supplied map, but does not implement the numeric sorting shown by its comment example. Producer repeats del/detachTo parameters and native multipart matching pairs them by index. Original code unescapes the entire query before manual field extraction; accepted code uses URLParams. The later ampersand-directory test directly checks the external URL; no malformed/duplicate/nested/query execution ran.",
        "deleteAttachments JSDoc reverses the silent Boolean: code confirms only if !silent. Several async return docs still name bare string/null rather than promise results. Historical non-silent detach saves through saveAttachments then unconditionally saves each again; accepted code saves in the silent branch only and uses the shared filename map. No save/detach/file picker/native IMAP operation was executed.",
        "Current saveAttachments can skip a file after overwrite refusal and still return the directory. detachAttachments receives only that directory and builds a full attachments map; the return value therefore is not proof every requested file was written. No skipped-overwrite detachment, data-loss outcome or UI effect was reproduced. Copy temporary-file cleanup runs after awaited success, not in a general error cleanup block.",
        "Full Bug1788159 edited description/comments0–9, updates and footer read. Early API/ownership/listener notes are proposals, not the final design. Comment3 limits the first JS rewrite to one WOPrompts path. Comment7 lands these first two patches; comment8 reopens because lint prevented landing the whole stack, not because these two were backed out; comment9 lands later detachAll/saveAll removals separately. Later regression IDs are metadata only. No linked regressions, Try jobs or runtime results were audited by association.",
        "D253184 complete creation-to-final summary/timeline and all eight actual inline bodies are read. The null-path suggestion matches the actual deletion map values; the stripAttachments JSDoc still says undefined, so a Done label does not make the docs consistent. Square brackets are explained as optional parameter syntax; no new project-wide naming policy follows.",
        "Reviewer suggests an IMAP-specific helper name. The author keeps generic updateFolder in anticipation of other protocols; current actual guard still returns for every non-IMAP folder. This is a declined naming premise/future direction, not implemented EWS refresh support. The temporary saveFirst IDL ambiguity is acknowledged while its later removal is deferred to another stack patch.",
        "Author multi-parameter parsing rationale matches the repeated del/detachTo source bridge. Historical Good try/build-completion notices are attributed reports. All new source findings remain supported from public Git only: full promise completion versus earlier key notification, paired native part/path indexing, and the save-directory/per-file-success distinction. Current ampersand regression test and complete API retirement are later accepted comparison context, not extra chronological audit credit."
